description: The museum's flagship and the oldest aircraft in Honduras. The museum states it entered the country in 1935 under the government of General Tiburcio Carías Andino and was registered in 1937 — the two dates are inconsistent and neither is a documented construction date; so year_built is deliberately blank. The museum claims it is possibly the only complete example of its type in the world with all original parts. It last flew at the Fuerza Aérea Hondureña's 50th anniversary in 1981 and was restored in 2002 before the museum opened. English Wikipedia lists the same airframe as an NA-42.

Bureau Number 124715. Delivered to the US Navy; then transferred to the Fuerza Aérea Hondureña as FAH-609 in March 1956; in FAH service until 1980. This is the aircraft flown by Captain (later Colonel) Fernando Soto Henríquez "El Flaco" on 17 July 1969 during the Football War; when he shot down two Salvadoran FG-1D Corsairs and a Cavalier F-51D Mustang — the last aerial combat between piston-engine fighters in history. It carries three kill markings for those victories. On display at the museum since 1990; a restoration began in 2012 and it is now displayed under cover. Armament shown as four 20 mm cannon with bombs and rockets. Silverhawkauthor gives the sub-type as F4U-5NL and the name "The Weak Spot"; neither is corroborated elsewhere; so the name field is left blank. Most recent photographic evidence located: airhistory.net image dated 2 March 2011; plus a dated site visit reported October 2022.
aliases: F4U5N; F4U-5N; F4U-5NL; Corsair; Corsario; BuNo 124715; 124715
